about.title: Del Rey Oaks Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Del Rey Oaks is a small city, but its traffic corridors carry plenty of pass-through and commuter volume, especially where Canyon Del Rey Boulevard meets Rt 68 and General Jim Moore Boulevard near Rt 218. Reported collisions in this area tend to cluster on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., often tied to commute and errand traffic converging at these junctions. Whether your crash happened on a state route or a quieter residential street, the days right after a collision matter. Insurance adjusters may call quickly, sometimes before you've seen a doctor or understood the full scope of your injuries. LawProactive doesn't practice law or negotiate claims; we simply connect injured people in Del Rey Oaks with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate your situation, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid common missteps with insurers. The connection is free, and any attorney you work with is paid only if you recover compensation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government entity's road or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Missing it can end your claim, so it helps to understand which deadline applies to you early.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the collision, though your share of blame reduces the payout. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you before you settle.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash; you're not required to give one, and what you say can be used to minimize your claim later. It's worth speaking with an attorney first so your words aren't taken out of context.

items.question: Do I have a case if the crash happened at Canyon Del Rey Boulevard and Rt 68?
items.answer: Having a case depends on the facts of your specific crash, not just the location. An independent attorney can review the details, including any police report or witness information from that intersection, and let you know your options. There's no cost to have your situation looked at.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to seek compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't be barred outright. An attorney can help assess how fault might be allocated in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a car accident in Del Rey Oaks?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. That period can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government vehicle or road defect was involved. Because these deadlines are strict, it's best to explore your options sooner rather than later.
